conclusion: You have two copies of the ε2 version of the APOE gene, which is rare: fewer than 1 in 100 people have it. The APOE gene comes in three common versions, called ε2, ε3 and ε4. They differ from each other at two places in the gene, and everyone carries two versions, one from each parent. APOE helps carry cholesterol and other fats in the blood and the brain. This combination is linked with the lowest APOE-related risk of Alzheimer's disease. A small share of people with it develop a cholesterol disorder called dysbetalipoproteinaemia, usually only together with something else such as weight gain or diabetes. A standard blood cholesterol test would show it.

You have one ε2 and one ε3 version of the APOE gene. About 1 in 8 people of European ancestry have this combination. The APOE gene comes in three common versions, called ε2, ε3 and ε4. They differ from each other at two places in the gene, and everyone carries two versions, one from each parent. APOE helps carry cholesterol and other fats in the blood and the brain. The ε2 version is linked with a somewhat lower risk of Alzheimer's disease that starts late in life than two ε3 copies. The effect is modest, and age, other genes and health matter more.

You have one ε2 and one ε4 version of the APOE gene. About 2 in 100 people of European ancestry have this combination. The APOE gene comes in three common versions, called ε2, ε3 and ε4. They differ from each other at two places in the gene, and everyone carries two versions, one from each parent. APOE helps carry cholesterol and other fats in the blood and the brain. The two versions pull in opposite directions: ε4 raises the risk of Alzheimer's disease that starts late in life and ε2 lowers it. They do not simply cancel out; studies suggest a moderately raised risk overall, but they disagree, so treat this result with caution.

You have two copies of the ε3 version of the APOE gene, the most common combination: about 6 in 10 people of European ancestry have it, and it is common everywhere. The APOE gene comes in three common versions, called ε2, ε3 and ε4. They differ from each other at two places in the gene, and everyone carries two versions, one from each parent. APOE helps carry cholesterol and other fats in the blood and the brain. Studies of APOE and Alzheimer's disease measure risk against this combination, so your APOE result puts you at the usual, average level of APOE-related risk, neither raised nor lowered. For any one person, age, other genes and health matter far more than this result.

You have one ε4 version (often called APOE4) and one ε3 version of the APOE gene. About 1 in 5 people of European ancestry have this combination. The APOE gene comes in three common versions, called ε2, ε3 and ε4. They differ from each other at two places in the gene, and everyone carries two versions, one from each parent. APOE helps carry cholesterol and other fats in the blood and the brain. The ε4 version is the best-known genetic factor for Alzheimer's disease that starts late in life: on average, one copy raises the risk about two to three times compared with two ε3 copies. Most people with one copy never develop Alzheimer's, and the effect varies with age, sex and ancestry. A genetic counsellor can explain what this does and does not mean for you.

You have two copies of the ε4 version of the APOE gene (often called APOE4). About 2 in 100 people of European ancestry have this combination. The APOE gene comes in three common versions, called ε2, ε3 and ε4. They differ from each other at two places in the gene, and everyone carries two versions, one from each parent. APOE helps carry cholesterol and other fats in the blood and the brain. Two ε4 copies carry the highest APOE-related risk of Alzheimer's disease that starts late in life, several times the average, and symptoms, when they come, tend to start earlier. It is still not a certainty: some people with two copies never develop the disease. Because this result can weigh on people, a genetic counsellor or doctor is the right person to put it in context.
